items.prompt: A hospital wants to predict which admitted patients will need intensive care, using five years of labelled admission records. Which problem formulation fits?

options.label: a
options.text: Nothing — the model was measured on data it had already seen.

options.label: b
options.note: The core misconception the course targets: memorisation being read as generalisation.
options.text: It is valid, because the model still had to learn the pattern.

options.label: c
options.note: Believes leakage is diluted by scale rather than invalidating the measure.
options.text: It is valid if the dataset is large enough.

items.prompt: A student reports 99% accuracy. You then learn the same rows appear in both the training and the test set. What is the accuracy figure worth?

items.answer_key: Search fits when states, actions and a goal test can be stated explicitly. It does not fit when the mapping must be induced from examples because no goal test is available.
items.marking_guidance: Full marks require the distinguishing criterion, not just two examples.
items.prompt: Give one problem that can be formulated as state-space search and one that cannot, and say what distinguishes them.

items.answer_key: The problem formulation determines the method family; the algorithm is chosen within it, against data and constraints.
items.marking_guidance: Accept any answer that puts problem structure before algorithm choice and gives a reason.
items.prompt: You are asked to choose between a method family and a specific algorithm. Which decision comes first, and why?

outcomes.description: The student can classify a problem as search, optimisation, supervised learning or unsupervised learning, and can explain which family of methods applies.
outcomes.title: Explain core AI problem types and methods
